assumptions: L(n) computed by the split-first greedy strategy, which is optimal by Cusenza et al. (2022, Thm 1.2) and was confirmed independently for n <= 150 (EXP-C19-01)
levels j: F = 1, 2, 3, 5, ... (level j carries FIB[j])
falsification: Any n contradicting H-C19-F or H-C19-R; the additive models are refuted by explicit counterexamples or inconsistent linear systems.
hypothesis: H-C19-F: D(F at level j) = floor(j^2/4). H-C19-1 (bold): D is additive over Zeckendorf summands up to a correction for consecutive pairs only. H-C19-2: the effect of the top summand depends only on the two highest levels. H-C19-3 (bold): D is additive over the runs of the lazy representation. H-C19-R: D(F_j + m) = floor(j^2/4) + D(m) - rho_(j mod 2)(m) with the explicit rho of systems/zeckendorf_game.py (inferred from n < 30000; out-of-sample tests in EXP-C19-04).
methodology: Greedy lengths for all n < 30000 and for Fibonacci inputs up to level 33; two-summand values for j <= 24; exact rational rank test for the lazy-run model on n < 160; comparison of the recursion with the greedy on n < 30000.
question: How does D(n) = B(n) - L(n) (B = sum_i a_i delta_i, Cusenza et al.) depend on the Zeckendorf digits of n?
